data.name: Aana
data.gender_notes: Aana is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'anā', meaning 'to hope' or 'to wish'. In Islamic tradition, Aana is a name of the beloved Prophet Muhammad's (pbuh) daughter, Fatima (ra). It is also used as a term of endearment and a symbol of love and devotion. The name Aana carries the meaning “Hope, Wish” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Aana usually hope their child will grow to embody hope, wish and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name filled with hope and love, evoking a deep sense of connection to the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and his daughter Fatima (ra).
data.etymology: Aana belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Hope, Wish.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aana total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

historical_references.context: Ibn Battuta was a renowned traveler from Morocco who explored Asia and Africa in the 14th century. He made a note of a city called Aana in his travelogue.

historical_references.reference: Aana was also known as 'Ana or 'Amna in medieval Arabic texts, and was an important trading center between Egypt and Nubia.
historical_references.context: Aana was a significant city in the Nile Valley, located between the regions of Egypt and Nubia. It served as a major trading center and played an essential role in the exchange of goods between these two civilizations.
